subject: Successive summarise calls plyr vs. dplyr?

messages.author: 146c5031f31e4913
messages.subject: Successive summarise calls plyr vs. dplyr?
parts:
I recently ran into the following issue I can't decide if it's unexpected behavior, or not. Sometimes I want to run successive summarise calls on data. Summarising by say 3 levels, and then taking a sub-summary of that data by summarising again, with only one of the levels. Under the plyr paradigm I never had an issue, so in making the switch to dplyr, this could be bug or simply a bad programming habit on my part.

A reproducible example:

library(plyr)
library(dplyr)
library(Lahman)

## using plyr

one <- ddply(Batting, .(playerID, yearID, teamID), summarise,
             total = sum(G))

two <- ddply(one, .(yearID), summarise,
             total = sum(total))

## using dplyr

three <- Batting %.%
         group_by(playerID, yearID, teamID) %.%
         summarise(total = sum(G))

four  <- three %.%
         group_by(yearID) %.%
         summarise(total = sum(total))

Can anyone tell me why data frames two and four end up differently?

Thank you, 

Jake

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Successive summarise calls plyr vs. dplyr?
parts:
Because dplyr::summarise() preserves the grouping, peeling only one
layer of grouping off each time.

Hadley

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Successive summarise calls plyr vs. dplyr?
parts:
Either set the groups with group_by(..., add = FALSE), remove the
groups with ungroup(), or most naturally, summarise the originally
ungrouped data.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Successive summarise calls plyr vs. dplyr?
parts:
Sure. Basically Hadley told me to use group_by's "add" option.

So to fix my issue just change the last call to

four  <- three %.%
         group_by(yearID, add = FALSE) %.%
         summarise(total = sum(G))

That gives the equivalent "two" data frame from the plyr commands above.
